title: Day 16 in my management game. The hardest about making a game, is testing it.
author: bahaw1024
selftext:
Each day is roughly about 8 minutes real time. 

8 x 16 = 128 minutes each time i want get to this point. How do other sims test long hours of testing? I have plenty of unit tests but something like balancing I won't be able to find until I just play play play. 

I've hired a few play testers, like 5 so far. Averaging an hour of game play for about $10/$15 

This current run i m on is the longest so far. In the past i would get to a day a notice a huge blocking bug and would go back and fix it and then start again. 



If anyone wants to playtest it [https://bahawludba.itch.io/hookah-house](https://bahawludba.itch.io/hookah-house) ( I can DM the pass)

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4607750/Hookah\_House/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4607750/Hookah_House/)

**TLDR: Should I automate some e2e testing? playwright? or just keep manual testing?**

comments.author: bahaw1024
comments.body: Opps clearly I am still waking up; I meant 'the hardest thing'

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
I was looking at puccas resturaunt I used to play a shiiit load just last night thinking of attempting to make something similar. 

But here we go a very good reskin replica 
Well done

replies.author: bahaw1024
replies.body: Oh, that's awesome. I had not heard of that game until you've mentioned it here. I looked it up and it looks pretty similar as you said. I've actually been told by a close friend that he would enjoy the game more on mobile because it's point-and-click as well. If you'd like to play my game just for fun with no expectations to play test or anything, please let me know. I'll be more than happy to give you a free download.

comments.author: Tom_Baron
comments.body: Why is playing a game you created a chore? Ai can do everything but create and develop a fun idea. If your game isnt fun and you're paying people to test it and complaining about play testing it, you have nothing.

replies.author: bahaw1024
replies.body: It's definitely not a chore. I think I misrepresented myself. What I'm trying to ask is the game is really fun and I've spent hours and hours and hours and hours and six months developing it and testing it, and I want to keep doing that. But I'm trying to figure out that can't be the only right way to test for small bugs. Just trying to figure out if there is an automated way with Playwright to do point and click testing.

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
Also why aren't you setting up a full game test suite you can run after making changes 

That's what I do , every single function call has a test flag 

Built into categories 

And big changes runs a full suite 
Small changes only run category based suites 


Barely any bugs pop up this way

replies.author: bahaw1024
replies.body: We do something similar but just run everything every time. About 3,800 unit tests, and after every code change it compile checks all the scripts and runs the full suite automatically, around 40 seconds total. If anything fails it has to get fixed before moving on. CI runs it again on every push. I also have about 100 scripted tests that play a feature in a real game session and check it, but those I run by hand. Where yours goes further is the per-function flags. I don't have a test for every function, just per feature and for every bug fix, so that's the part I think I can do from your advicr :)

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Yea mine has headless play run tests aswell with a test room 

Pretty similar to yours 

But I prefer having above normal amounts of tests to test every single action and reaction 
And function calls if it does work or does not 

Saves me a ton of manual play testing 
But I still do manual ones just to sort out visual aspects

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
You separate the simulation from the visuals and then the AI can run the game at very high speed purely as a simulation. I managed 20 test runs of 7 days each in about 5 minutes for my previous game.

In the end, you do need to do the play test to find the UI and UX bugs that might appear but stability and balance testing should be automated as much as possible.
